description: What omarchy-m-test expects of each feature, per chip generation, in three layers: Asahi hardware features, Aurora additions and Omarchy integration. Results are classified against Aurora's expected state first, then Asahi's. Edited by pull request; bump catalogue_version on every change.

asahi.title: Asahi Linux feature support
asahi.credit: Asahi-layer states are from the Asahi Linux documentation's feature-support tables (m1.md, m2.md, m3.md, m4.md), (c) the Asahi Linux contributors, licensed under CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Converted from table cells to per-chip states; unmodified cell text is kept in each state's "cell".

aurora.title: Aurora kernel (omacom/linux) and omarchy-mx-mac's hardware support page
aurora.note: Aurora additions as of kernel 7.1.12, qualified on the MacBook Pro 14" M1 Pro (j314s) and 16" M2 Max (j416c). Aurora status "asahi" means Aurora is expected to match linux-asahi for that feature, not independently verified.

outcomes.fails: doesn't work, but should on this Mac
outcomes.not-applicable: this Mac doesn't have this hardware

features.name: Thunderbolt

aurora.evidence: Not yet seen working on a real M1. M1 Pro, fresh converged image on linux-aurora 7.1.12, 2026-09-27, nothing but a charger attached: thunderbolt-apple-acio binds the three ports and every cold boot logs 'thunderbolt-apple-acio 701ac0000.cio: PCIe-C tunnel disabled: m1n1 handoff is not initialized' (and for b01ac0000.cio, f01ac0000.cio); no Thunderbolt domain registers, as expected with no USB4/Thunderbolt partner (tests/corpus/m1-pro-converged-fresh). The earlier M1 corpus domains are reconstructed stand-ins.

Not yet seen working on a real M1. M1 Pro, fresh converged image on linux-aurora 7.1.12, 2026-09-27, nothing but a charger attached: thunderbolt-apple-acio binds the three ports and every cold boot logs 'thunderbolt-apple-acio 701ac0000.cio: PCIe-C tunnel disabled: m1n1 handoff is not initialized' (and for b01ac0000.cio, f01ac0000.cio); no Thunderbolt domain registers, as expected with no USB4/Thunderbolt partner (tests/corpus/m1-pro-converged-fresh). The earlier M1 corpus domains are reconstructed stand-ins.

features.note: Partial in Aurora. thunderbolt-apple-acio and thunderbolt-apple-nhi bring the USB4/Thunderbolt host up once the Type-C PHY is in USB4/Thunderbolt mode, so a domain only exists while a USB4 or Thunderbolt partner is attached (ports.thunderbolt skips an idle Mac). On M2 that host works: domains, links to devices and to other computers over thunderbolt-net, which is what ports.thunderbolt checks. PCIe tunnels (docks' PCIe devices, eGPUs) aren't there on M1 or M2: every cold boot logs 'thunderbolt-apple-acio 701ac0000.cio: PCIe-C tunnel disabled: m1n1 handoff is not initialized' (drivers/thunderbolt/apple.c in omacom/linux), a known limit until m1n1 hands the tunnels over. On M1 the host hasn't been seen working yet (see the aurora evidence), so a failure there is an expected gap.

features.name: DisplayPort alt mode
features.note: Aurora adds DP alt mode on M1 and M2; see usb4-displays.

features.name: DisplayPort audio
features.note: Not a row in Asahi's feature tables: the display coprocessor's DisplayPort audio (apple,*-dpaudio) has no Asahi driver yet.

features.name: External displays over USB-C (DP alt mode and USB4)
features.note: Several external displays through USB-C, up to five on the M2 Max.

features.name: Variable refresh rate (ProMotion)
features.note: ProMotion on the 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro built-in displays.

features.name: Always-on processor (AOP: ambient light sensor, lid angle)
features.note: Not confirmed on the base M1 (t8103).

features.name: A driver for every hardware node
features.note: From the hardware inventory: every enabled device-tree node with a device of its own should have a driver bound, and none should fail its probe. Aurora doesn't claim that on any chip yet; each report lists what's unclaimed.

features.name: Kernel build options (compared with Asahi's)
features.note: The running kernel's /proc/config.gz compared with Asahi's reference configuration (catalogue/asahi-kernel/). Differences are reported, not judged: Aurora builds more than Asahi on purpose.

features.name: Bar clear of the notch
features.note: Waybar laid out around the camera notch on MacBook Pro 14/16 and MacBook Air (M2 and later).

features.name: Clamshell mode (lid closed with an external display)
features.note: Closing the lid with an external display attached keeps the session on the external display instead of suspending.

features.name: Automatic keyboard backlight
features.note: Keyboard backlight follows the ambient light sensor.

features.name: Speaker protection
features.note: speakersafetyd active and the WirePlumber convolver chain loaded before anything plays.

features.name: First join to a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network
features.note: Known issue: the first join after the Wi-Fi driver starts can land on the network's 6 GHz radio on BCM4388 Macs and get no traffic; a retry connects. omarchy-mac's iwd band preference avoids it (omacom/omarchy-mac#573).

features.name: First-boot hardware setup
features.note: omarchy-mac's first-boot hardware setup completes, including offline.

features.name: Boot chain
features.note: The installed kernel package is the running one, and omarchy-mac's boot check finds m1n1, U-Boot and Limine (or GRUB) and their boot files as installed.

features.name: Disk encryption
features.note: The root filesystem is on a LUKS volume the boot chain unlocked.

features.name: Package repositories
features.note: pacman is configured with the repositories the Mac needs, and one of them carries the running kernel's package.

features.name: Vendor firmware
features.note: omarchy-vendor-firmware.service installs the Apple firmware copied from macOS in each boot.

features.name: System services
features.note: No system or user unit has failed.

features.name: Snapshots
features.note: /.snapshots is a btrfs subvolume snapper keeps snapshots in.

features.name: iwd Wi-Fi backend
features.note: NetworkManager drives the Broadcom Wi-Fi through iwd.

features.name: Microphone mapping
features.note: omarchy-mac's omarchy-asahi-mic.service maps the Asahi DSP microphone array to a stereo default source.

features.name: Firmware for every driver that asks
features.note: No firmware-load failure in this boot's kernel log: the firmware drivers ask for is installed (vendor firmware from macOS, linux-firmware and Asahi's firmware packages such as avd-fw).

features.name: Battery charge limit kept across reboots
features.note: omarchy-mac's `omarchy battery charge limit [80|100]` sets the SMC's charge limit and saves it to /etc/udev/macsmc-battery.conf; its udev rule restores the saved limit when the battery appears at boot.
